note: Written; validate_items.R --table-sets passes (36/36 items, resp 0-8 exact). Caveats. (1) SHAPE: an 'item' here is NOT a question. The child gave one free-text answer per stimulus, and two trained coders, blind to the hypotheses and to participant demographics, scored how many expressions in that answer fell into each of nine disability-model categories; the live resp is that raw count, 0-8. So section_prompt carries the question the child was actually asked (the four stimulus questions from the Child's Protocol) and item_text carries the S2 File's own verbatim coding criterion for the category being counted (criteria list 1..9, transcribed with the list number dropped). There is no per-item stem to transcribe, and no response-option labels exist at all: resp is a count, so option_text is blank for all nine levels rather than padded with the level's own number. This is disclosed in public_note. (2) CHILD PROTOCOL, not the parent one: the S2 File carries a separate Parent's Protocol version of this open-ended questionnaire and it was deliberately NOT used. The instructions differ entirely (parents: 'Imagine that your child has asked you the following question ... Please write a brief answer.', self-administered in writing; children: an oral interview script, 'I am going to ask you some questions ... What do you think makes his or her life difficult?'), and stimulus (iii) differs by one word -- the child protocol reads 'Paolo is autistic and does not understand what others say', the parent protocol 'and he does not understand'. The child reading ships. data/meloni_2015_disability.py splits child from parent by ROW (Protocol 200-299), not by column, so the S1 columns are shared with meloni_2015_deq_oe_parent and the protocol version is the only thing that distinguishes the two tables' text. (3) Administered in Italian to 76 Italian primary-school children interviewed at home in Perugia by the author Fabio Meloni; the deposit publishes no Italian wording anywhere (S2 re-checked this round: the only non-ASCII characters in the whole converted codebook are typographic punctuation -- no accented characters, no Italian text; S1 is a single-sheet SPSS-exported .xls holding numbers and a bare ASCII header row, 153 x 244). So the authors' own English ships in the base fields with language=Italian and the four _translated columns empty: text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. (4) mapping_basis=paper_order, Step 5b routes 3 + 8, status PARTIAL (see verification file). The item code IS the S1 column name -- data/meloni_2015_disability.py melts every column starting DEQ_OE with no rename and no positional step, core-model derivation pattern 1 -- and the S1 .xls carries no variable or value labels, so no data_labels route exists for this deposit. What route 3 settles decisively is the macro-model membership of the nine suffixes and the identity of the able-bodied stimulus; what it does not settle is the order within {Eth, Est, Rel} or the MD-vs-SD pair. (5) TRANSCRIPTION DEVIATIONS, all disclosed: typographic apostrophes and quotation marks rendered as ASCII; the leading list number stripped from each of the nine criteria ('1. Ethical Model: ...' ships as 'Ethical Model: ...'); the source's double full stop in criterion 7 ('...(health or disease)..') is shipped verbatim, uncorrected. Nothing else was altered -- in particular the instructions keep the study's own placeholder 'the Target Item [Target Item description]' rather than substituting a stimulus name. correct_response is blank throughout: a free-text explanation has no key, and the processing script performs no correct/incorrect recode. (6) RIGHTS: no block. The instrument is the authors' own -- the article states the questionnaires 'maintained the same format as the questionnaires that Evans [35] used, i.e., item number, item type (open or closed questions), Likert scale ranges, and open-ended questionnaire coding system. However, the item content, instructions, and questionnaire stimuli were modified' -- and both the questions and the coding criteria are published by them in the S2 File of a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article ('Copyright: (c) 2015 Meloni et al. ... Creative Commons Attribution License, which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium'). itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv was checked row by row (33 rows) by instrument name and by family: no row matches, and no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause is quotable for this instrument on the article or supplement pages. (7) STEP 3b: matches. 36 live items named DEQ_OE_<MD|SD|CD|ND>_<9 model suffixes> on integer resp 0-8 with n = 76 on every item -- exactly the DEQ_OE block of the deposit restricted to the 76 child respondents, and not one of the five other measures in the same file (DEQ*_CE_* is the closed-ended counterpart on 1-4 with half points, HK*/IA*/PE*/CHIA* are the other questionnaires). (8) PROVENANCE OF THIS ROUND: itemtext/quarantine/batch_102/ holds a 324-row extraction of this table from a killed round with no provenance row. It was consulted as a lead only; the item set, the wording, the mapping and the verification were re-established from the deposit this round (S1 header re-read, S2 re-converted section re-read, Fig 1 fetched and read directly), and the shipped CSV was rebuilt from the codebook text programmatically rather than promoted.
public_note: These 36 'items' are not questions: each child gave one free-text answer to each of four stimulus questions (a man in a wheelchair, a blind woman, an autistic child, an able-bodied woman), and two blind coders then counted how many expressions in that answer fell into each of nine disability-model categories, so the response is a count of coded mentions and has no response-option labels; the question the child was asked is given as the section prompt and the item text is the study's own verbatim coding criterion for the category being counted. The interviews were conducted in Italian with Italian primary-school children and neither the article nor its supplements publish any Italian wording, so everything shown here is the English of the study's own S2 File codebook.

note: mapping_basis=paper_explicit. data/meloni_2015_disability.py subsets the S1 workbook to Protocol 101-199 (parents) and melts the 36 DEQ_OE_* columns by name with no rename and no positional step -- core-model derivation pattern 1 -- so the IRW item code IS the S1 column name. NO data_labels route exists: the S1 .xls was opened again this round -- one sheet, Dataset_S1, no variable labels and no value labels anywhere, only a bare ASCII header row. What ties each code to text is the S2 codebook, and it does it by NAME rather than by order alone: the code's second half is the stimulus block (MD/SD/CD/ND) and the third is an abbreviation of one of the nine coding categories the codebook enumerates -- Eth/Est/Rel/Med/Env/SRel/Bio/Oth/Idont against '(i) ethical model, (ii) aesthetic model, (iii) religious model, (iv) medical model, (v) environmental model, (vi) socio-relational model, (vii) biopsychosocial model, (viii) other, (ix) I don't know', which is also the exact left-to-right order of the S1 columns and of Table 1A's own grid. Table 1A likewise labels its rows 'Motor / Sensory / Intellectual', matching MD/SD/CD, with ND the fourth, non-disability stimulus (Elena). WHAT AN 'ITEM' IS HERE, and it is not an administered probe: parents wrote a free-text answer to each of four questions, and two blind coders then assigned each answer to one of nine disability-model categories. The 36 IRW items are those 4 stimuli x 9 categories, and resp is a count of coded mentions (0-5), so item_text names the CODING CATEGORY while the administered wording sits in instructions and section_prompt. This is disclosed in the public_note; no per-item stem was invented. option_text is blank for every row: the respondent chose nothing, the counts carry no labels, and padding a count with its own number is forbidden. correct_response is blank -- there is no key. PARENT vs CHILD: the S2 File carries a separate Child's Protocol version and it is the PARENT one that ships. (1) The instructions are entirely different -- the parents' is a written self-administered rubric ('Imagine that your child has asked you the following question ... Please write a brief answer'), not the child protocol's spoken script ('I am going to ask you some questions ... What do you think makes his or her life difficult?'). (2) All four questions were diffed against the child form character by character: exactly one differs, (iii), which reads 'Paolo is autistic and he does not understand what others say' for parents against '...and does not understand what others say' for children; the parent reading ships. VERIFICATION: Step 5b routes 3 + 8, status PARTIAL, re-runnable as verify_meloni_2015_deq_oe_parent.R (VERDICT: PASS, 8/8 checks). Route 3: Fig 1 prints the parents' mean frequency preference for the individual / social / biopsychosocial models as 1.9 / 1.39 / 0.14 on S2 Table 1A's 0-3 presence scale, and the shipped category grouping summed over the three DISABILITY stimuli reproduces them as 1.9079 / 1.3947 / 0.1447 (max error 0.0079); the three rival triples that treat ND as a disability condition miss by 0.163-0.272. That pins ND as the able-bodied stimulus and the {Eth,Est,Rel,Med} / {Env,SRel} / {Bio} grouping. Route 8 adds four content checks that follow from the category names: Aesthetic is coded only under ND (0.000/0.000/0.000/0.053), 'I don't know' is never coded for parents (0.000 everywhere, matching S2's 'usually more common in children than in adults'), Environmental peaks at the wheelchair stimulus and bottoms at the autistic one (MD 0.461 > SD 0.303 > CD 0.171) while Socio-Relational peaks at the autistic one (CD 0.461), and Medical peaks at the blind stimulus (SD 1.026) and is lowest for the able-bodied one (ND 0.355). The live table is tied to the deposit by a per-item fingerprint -- n / resp_min / resp_max / n_resp_levels for all 36 codes, 36/36 exact, via irw::irw_table_sets() so nothing was exported. NOT established: the order within {Ethical, Religious, Medical} or within {Environmental, Socio-relational}, or Other vs I-don't-know, beyond those content checks; and MD/SD/CD are separated only by route-8 content ordering, not by a published per-condition number.
